headline: Approved a 41,000-square-foot Dartmouth Hitchcock addition at 251-253 Pleasant Street with conditions; continued the Steeplegate redevelopment to October 21.
summary: The meeting approved a major site plan, waivers, and a height permit for a 41,000-square-foot addition to Dartmouth Hitchcock Medical Center at 251-253 Pleasant Street. It also approved signs, a site plan extension for 270 Loudon Rd, and a solar array at 52-54 Portsmouth Street. It recommended that City Council adopt four zoning amendments and continued the Steeplegate redevelopment and several other applications.
decisions: Approved the minutes of the July 15, 2026 and July 21, 2026 meetings, 8-0-0.
Continued the two-unit condominium conversion at 3 Palm Street to September 16, 2026, 9-0-0.
Continued the car dealership site plan at 110 Manchester Street to September 16, 2026, 9-0-0.
Continued the 24-lot subdivision on Tax Map 8814Z Lot 4 to September 16, 2026, 9-0-0.
Approved sign items 5A through 5D as submitted, subject to Architectural Design Review Committee recommendations, 9-0-0.
Approved two signs at 154 North Main Street, with both signs non-illuminated.
Approved a blade sign at 26 Pleasant Street with an opaque background behind the white background.
Granted a second one-year extension for 270 Loudon Rd, moving the approval expiration to July 17, 2027, 9-0-0.
Approved signs at 376 Loudon Road with the drive-thru text changed to white, 9-0-0.
Continued the signs at 25 South Main Street to September 16, 2026, 9-0-0.
Approved signs at 92 South Street with the upper section of the pylon sign dimmed, 9-0-0.
Granted conditional use permit for a Kimball Jenkins wall sign above first-floor window sills at 264 North Main Street, 9-0-0.
Granted a waiver to allow timber curbing at 52-54 Portsmouth Street, 9-0-0.
Approved an amendment to the site plan for a ground-mounted solar array at 52-54 Portsmouth Street, 9-0-0.
Granted ten site plan waivers for the 251 Pleasant Street addition, 9-0-0.
Denied a waiver from the full traffic study requirement for 251 Pleasant Street, 9-0-0.
Granted conditional use permit for rooftop mechanical equipment above the height limit at 251 Pleasant Street, 9-0-0.
Granted architectural design review for the 41,000-square-foot addition at 251-253 Pleasant Street, 9-0-0.
Granted major site plan approval for the 41,000-square-foot addition at 251-253 Pleasant Street, subject to conditions, 9-0-0.
Continued the comprehensive development plan for the former Steeplegate Mall and Regal Cinema sites to October 21, 2026, 9-0-0.
Determined the design review phase of the mixed-use redevelopment application is complete.
Recommended City Council adopt zoning amendments to parking, loading, and driveway access rules, 9-0-0.
Scheduled a public hearing on Site Plan Regulation amendments for September 16, 2026 at 7 p.m., 9-0-0.
Recommended City Council adopt zoning amendments on nonconforming structures and subdivisions, 9-0-0.
Recommended City Council adopt updated arterial and collector street lists, 9-0-0.
Recommended City Council adopt updated federal flood insurance maps in the zoning overlay maps, 9-0-0.
Confirmed the September 19, 2026 master plan visioning session, starting at 9 a.m., 8-1-0.

City of Concord Planning Board 
August 19, 2026  
 Minutes 
 
 
1 
 
 
The regular monthly meeting of the Concord Planning Board was held on August 19, 2026, at 7:00 p.m., 
in City Council Chambers at 37 Green St, Concord. 
 
Attendees:   Dina Condodemetraky, David Fox, Matthew Hicks, Alternate Leon LaFreniere, Teresa 
Rosenberger (Ex-Officio for City Manager), Amanda Savage, Eaton Tarbell, Councilor 
Brent Todd, Paige Wilber and Chair Richard Woodfin 
 
Absent:   Alternate Frank Kenison 
 
Staff: Tim Thompson – (Assistant Director of Community Development / Acting City Planner), 
Alec Bass (Assistant City Planner – Community Planning), Krista Tremblay 
(Administrative Technician III), Peter Kohalmi (Associate City Engineer), and Matt 
Walsh (Deputy City Manager – Development) 
 
 
1. Call to Order 
Chair Woodfin called the meeting to order at 7:00 p.m. 
 
2. Roll Call 
Acting Clerk Thompson did the roll call, noting that a quorum is present. 
 
3. Approval of Meeting Minutes 
  On a motion made by Member Hicks, seconded by Member Wilber, the Planning Board voted 8-0-0 
to approve the July 15, 2026 and July 21, 2026, Planning Board meeting minutes, as written.  
 
Member Condodemetraky arrived at 7:01 p.m. 
 
4. Agenda Overview 
On a motion made by Member Savage, seconded by Member Hicks, the Planning Board voted 9-0-0 
to continue agenda items 8A to a date certain of September 16, 2026, at the request of the applicant.  
 
On a motion made by Member Hicks, seconded by Member Savage, the Planning Board voted 9-0-0 
to continue agenda items 8B to a date certain of September 16, 2026, at the request of the applicant.  
 
On a motion made by Member Hicks, seconded by Member Savage, the Planning Board voted 9-0-0 
to continue agenda items 8C to a date certain of September 16, 2026, at the request of the applicant.  
 
5. Architectural Design Review by Consent 
On a motion made by Member Condodemetraky, seconded by Member Hicks, the Board voted 9-0-0 
to approve agenda items 5A-5D as submitted, subject to the recommendations of the Architectural 
Design Review Committee.  
 
5A. Sousa Signs, LLC, on behalf of Price Automotive Sales & Service and D&J Realty Holdings, LLC, 
requests an architectural design review approval for a new 62.7-square-foot internally illuminated 
freestanding sign panel (SP-0777-2026), to replace an existing sign panel at 79 Manchester Street in 
the Highway Commercial (CH) District. (PL-ADR-2026-0182) (2026-051)
City of Concord Planning Board 
August 19, 2026  
 Minutes 
 
 
2 
 
 
 
 The Planning Board approved the application as submitted.  
 
5B. City Buffet, LLC, on behalf of Concord Re Property, LLC, requests architectural design review 
approvals for two new internally illuminated freestanding sign panels of 54.55-square-foot (SP-0794-
2026) and 35.51-square feet (SP-0795-2026) at 161 Loudon Road in the General Commercial (CG) 
District. (PL-ADR-2026-0190) (2026-064) 
The Planning Board approved the application as submitted.  
5C. NEOPCO Signs, on behalf of Concord Smoke Shop and Remi’s Block, LLC, requests architectural 
design review approvals for a new 5.5-square-foot internally illuminated projecting blade sign (SP-
0806-2026), and a new 11-square-foot internally illuminated building wall sign (SP-0807-2026) at 
154 North Main Street in the Central Business Performance (CBP) District. (PL-ADR-2026-0193) 
(2026-073) 
The Planning Board approved the application as submitted with the understanding that both signs 
will be non-illuminated.  
 
5D. NEOPCO Signs, on behalf of Hvizda Reality Group and HRG Invests, LLC, requests an architectural 
design review approval for a new 9-square-foot internally illuminated blade sign panel (SP-0813-
2026) to replace an existing blade sign panel, at 26 Pleasant Street in the Central Business 
Performance (CBP) District. (PL-ADR-2026-0194) (2026-074). 
The Planning Board approved the application as submitted with the condition that an opaque 
background will be placed behind the white background leaving the red text and red sun to remain 
illuminated.  
 
5E. Signarama of Concord, on behalf of Uncle Charlie’s Eatery and TDL Investments LLC, request 
architectural design review approvals for a new 18.28-square-foot internally illuminated freestanding 
tenant panel sign (SP-0814-2026), to replace an existing tenant panel, and a new 33-square-foot 
internally illuminated building wall sign (SP-0815-2026), to replace an existing building wall sign, at 
376 Loudon Road in the Gateway Performance (GWP) District. (PL-ADR-2026-0195) (2026-076) 
Mr. Thompson stated agenda item 5E has been pulled from consent at the request of the applicant. 
Please see public hearings agenda item 5E.  
 
6.  Extension Requests by Consent  
 
6A. Gallagher, Callahan & Gartrell, PC, on behalf of Onyx Partners, Ltd, requests a second, one-year 
extension to the July 17, 2024, conditionally approved amendment to a major site plan, extending 
conditional approval expiration from July 17, 2026, to July 17, 2027, for 270 Loudon Rd, in the 
Gateway Performance (GWP) District. (2024-039) (PL-EXT-2026-0031) 
 
On a motion made by Member Hicks, seconded by Councilor Todd, the Board voted 9-0-0 to grant a 
second a one-year extension to the July 17, 2024, conditionally approved amendment to a major site 
plan, extending conditional approval expiration from July 17, 2026, to July 17, 2027, for 270 Loudon 
Rd, in the Gateway Performance (GWP) District.
City of Concord Planning Board 
August 19, 2026  
 Minutes 
 
 
3 
 
 
**End of Consent Agenda** 
 
Public Hearings 
5E. Signarama of Concord, on behalf of Uncle Charlie’s Eatery and TDL Investments LLC, request 
architectural design review approvals for a new 18.28-square-foot internally illuminated freestanding 
tenant panel sign (SP-0814-2026), to replace an existing tenant panel, and a new 33-square-foot 
internally illuminated building wall sign (SP-0815-2026), to replace an existing building wall sign, at 
376 Loudon Road in the Gateway Performance (GWP) District. (PL-ADR-2026-0195) (2026-076) 
Mr. Bass stated this sign application went to architectural design review committee and they 
recommended approval as submitted. The applicant since reached out and they have a minor revision 
to make to the sign. They are coming to the Board as a public hearing to show the revision and 
potentially grant architectural design review at this board meeting instead of having them come back 
through the process.  
Kendra Price (249 Sheep Davis Rd, Concord) presented the application. The client reached out to Ms. 
Price Monday to see if they can add the drive-thru portion on the pylon sign. Ms. Price noted it is still 
within the guidelines.   
Mr. Thompson noted the drive-thru portion of the sign was not reviewed by architectural design 
review committee and because of that this was pulled from consent so the Planning Board can 
consider whether or not the addition of the drive-thru signage is ok.  
Member Savage suggested note to have the red bar and having drive-thru with the arrow without the 
red. 
Ms. Price noted the existing sign for Morning Dew Coffee also had a similar bar with drive-thru and 
they were trying to incorporate the red from the leaf.   
Chair Woodfin noted the sign needs to differentiate a little bit.  
Member Rosenberger noted when you look at the sign it is the only drive-thru and it is ok to be in red 
with the yellow.  
 Ms. Price stated when she was going through the revision for the sign they did just the arrow and 
drive-thru in white with no banner and it blended in with the logo.  
Chair Woodfin asked if there was white text instead of the yellow text. 
Ms. Price noted that would work.  
Chair Woodfin asked if there is any member of the Board or audience that has questions or concerns 
about this application, with none, closed the public hearing. 
 
On a motion made by Member Savage, seconded by Member Fox, the Board voted 9-0-0 to approve 
the application as submitted with the condition that the yellow copy of “drive thru” be made 
white. 
 
7. Design Review Applications   
  
7A. Yamas Greek Eatery, on behalf of Yamas Greek Eatery and The Draft, LLC, requests architectural
City of Concord Planning Board

design review approvals for a 16-square-foot, externally illuminated existing non-permitted building 
wall sign (SP-0767-2026) and a new 1.77-square-foot non-illuminated projecting sign (SP-0792-
2026) at 25 South Main Street in the Central Business Performance (CBP) District. (PL-ADR-2026-
0179) (2026-047) 
 
Mr. Bass stated this application is non-conforming with zoning and they were to appear before the 
Zoning Board earlier this month, but were not present at the meeting, and were continued to the 
September ZBA meeting. The owner of this property has been contacted and is now aware of the 
schedule and process. Staff recommends continuing this application to the September 16 meeting so 
they can get the Zoning Board decision prior to a final decision by the Planning Board.  
 
Chair Woodfin asked if there is any member of the Board or audience that has questions or concerns 
about this application, with none, closed the public hearing. 
 
On a motion made by Member Hicks, seconded by Member Savage, the Board voted 9-0-0 to 
continue the application to the date certain of September 16, 2026. 
 
7B. NEOPCO Signs, on behalf of Capital Vision Center and Red Eagle Management, LLC, requests 
architectural design review approvals for a new 36-square-foot internally illuminated freestanding 
sign panel (SP-0797-2026), to replace an existing freestanding sign panel, and two new internally 
illuminated building walls signs of 74.75-square-feet (SP-0798-2026) and 49.78-square-feet (SP-
0799-2026) at 92 South Street in the Neighborhood Commercial (CN) District. (PL-ADR-2026-0192) 
(2026-070) 
 
Mr. Bass stated this application came before ADR and the recommendation was approval as 
submitted with the condition that an opaque background be provided behind the white of the pylon 
panel sign pursuant to Section 5.4(c) of the Design Review Guidelines, especially whereas this 
property abuts a residential district boundary. The applicant requested to be removed from consent 
and appear before the Planning Board.  
 
Glen Schadlick (5 Crosby St, Concord) presented the application. Mr. Schadlick noted disagreement 
with the ADRC recommendation to change the sign face from translucent to opaque. Mr. Schadlick 
presented his arguments as to why he believed that the design guidelines language is not mandatory 
and that the opaque background should not be required.  
  
Mr. Bass and Mr. Thompson discussed the construction and rationale for the regulatory requirements  
and guidelines, concluding that the Planning Board has broad discretionary decision making authority 
based on the guidelines and recommendations from ADR. They have been consistent over several 
years that when you have a white background that it is an opaque background as the recommendation 
for light pollution purposes.  
  
The Board, staff, and Mr. Schadlick continued to discuss the sign in the context of the neighborhood 
the regulatory standards, and recommendations of the ADRC, seeking to find a compromise position 
on the approval of the sign. 
 
There being no public testimony, Chair Woodfin closed the public hearing.
City of Concord Planning Board 
August 19, 2026  
 Minutes 
 
 
5 
 
 
On a motion made by Member Savage, seconded by Chair Woodfin, the Board voted 9-0-0 to 
approve the application as submitted with the condition that the upper section of the pylon sign 
(sign C in the application) be dimmed and that an opaque background be provided on the lower sign 
until such time that future tenant panel signs are provided which will either have a dark background 
with light copy, an opaque background be provided, or they too shall also be dimmed.  
 
8. Site Plan, Subdivision and Conditional Use Permit Applications 
8A. Eastern Development, on behalf of Ryan Taber, requests minor subdivision approval for a 2-unit 
condominium conversion at Tax Map 494 Lot 3, addressed as 3 Palm Street in the Neighborhood 
Residential (RN) District. (2026-026) (PL-MIS-2026-0049) (Applicant has requested to continue to 
date certain of September 16, 2026) 
 
This agenda item was continued to a date certain of September 16, 2026 in agenda item 4. 
 
8B. Wilcox & Barton Inc, on behalf of Two Wheeler Holdings, LLC, requests major site plan and 
architectural design review approvals for the conversion of an existing 30,310-square-foot building 
along with a 2,470-square-foot addition for a car dealership, 70,270-square-feet of additional

Park Performance (OFP) Districts. (2026-044) (PL-SPR-2026-0061) (Applicant has requested to 
continue to the date certain of September 16, 2026) 
 
This agenda item was continued to a date certain of September 16, 2026 in agenda item 4. 
 
8C. Nobis Group, on behalf of The Stabile Group, Bow Mills United Methodist Church, Inc, and D.

abutting property known as Tax Map 8814Z Lot 3, addressed as 271 South Street, in the Single 
Family Residential (RS) District. (2026-059) (PL-MAS-2026-0013) (Continued to September 16, 
2026, at the request of the applicant) 
 
This agenda item was continued to a date certain of September 16, 2026 in agenda item 4. 
 
8D. Kimball Jenkins, Inc, requests conditional use permit approval pursuant to Section 28-6-9(b)(2) and 
Section 28-6-7(i) of the Zoning Ordinance, to allow for a building wall sign to be located between 
rows of windows on a building that is 3 or more stories in height, above the sills of the first level of 
windows above the first story, or placed more than 25-feet above grade at Tax Map 641Z Lot 19, 
addressed as 264 North Main Street in the Neighborhood Residential (RN) District. (2026-075)(PL-
CUP-2026-0122) 
 
Mr. Thompson stated this application is for a conditional use permit for the proposed Kimball Jenkins 
signage on the south wall of the building, facing I-393.  Due to the grades in the area, Kimball 
Jenkins is requesting the sign be placed at a height above the sills of the first-floor windows.  The

 Minutes 
 
 
6 
 
 
Heritage Commission has already granted a certificate of approval for the signage (located in the 
Historic District).  City Staff is recommending acceptance of the application as complete, and 
following the public hearing recommend conditional approval of the CUP per the recommendations 
in the staff memo. 
 
On a motion made by Member Condodemetraky, seconded by Member Wilber the Board voted 8-0-0 
to determine the application complete and not a development of regional impact, per RSA 36:55. 
 
Chair Woodfin opened the public hearing.  
 
Chris Nadeau (18 Chenell Dr, Concord) presented the application. Mr. Nadeau noted you cannot see 
the estate and art school from the south and along 393. This sign is for people to see where the 
campus is located.  
 
There being no public testimony, Chair Woodfin closed the public hearing. 
 
Chair Woodfin stated the findings of fact include the information provided in the staff reports; the 
applicant’s submission materials; testimony provided during the public hearing; and/or other 
documents or materials provided in the public hearing.  
On a motion made by Member Tarbell, seconded by Member Hicks, the Board voted 9-0-0 to grant 
conditional use permit approval to allow the proposed signage placed above the sills of the first 
level of windows above the first story on the same wall, and/or placed more than twenty-five (25) feet

(a) Precedent Conditions – to be fulfilled within two years and prior to signature of the conditional

1. The applicant shall revise the conditional use permit plat to provide the Planning Board 
Approval Block on the 1-sheet, signage elevation plan and the 1-sheet sign site plan.  
2. Upon notification from the Planning Division that the project complies with the precedent 
conditions, Zoning Ordinance, and Site Plan Regulations, deliver to the Planning Division 
for signature two full-size or 11x17 conditional use permit plan sets.  
(b) Subsequent Conditions 
1. The applicant is responsible for compliance with the municipal code, Site Plan Regulations, 
and Construction Standards and Details, including obtaining necessary variances, waivers, 
and conditional use permits. 
 
8E. Nobis Group, on behalf of Society for the Protection of New Hampshire Forests, requests approval 
for an amendment to the previously approved 1999 Large Scale Development plan (1999-078) for the 
installation of a 102-Kw AC ground-mounted solar photovoltaic array as an accessory use to the 
existing conservation center, and certain associated site improvements at Tax Map 482Z Lot 14, 
addressed as 52-54 Portsmouth Street in the Open Space Residential (RO) District. (1999-078) (PL-
AMEND-2026-0024) 
 
Mr. Thompson stated this application would amend the Board’s 1999 approval for the SPNHF site, 
allowing for the installation of ground mounted solar and minor relocation of some required parking,
City of Concord Planning Board 
August 19, 2026  
 Minutes 
 
 
7 
 
 
resulting in a small increase to the amount of impervious surface on the site.  City Staff is conditional 
approval of the CUP per the recommendations in the staff memo. 
 
Chair Woodfin opened the public hearing. 
 
Morgan Dunson (18 Chenell Dr, Concord) presented the application. Ms. Dunson noted the site entry 
comes off the paved drive on Portsmouth St. Ms. Dunson is proposing to install solar arrays for the 
HVAC system to provide renewable energy on site. There is an existing conservation building and 
project area is in existing gravel parking lot. They are proposing to install solar panel arrays in the 
northern portion of the parking lot and they will need to reconfigure the parking lot to current 
standards. The impervious surface will increase by 295 square feet and that does not include the solar 
panels. There is a limited amount of tree clearing. The only earth work will be for the panels 
themselves. There are utilities an existing water and drain line. The new electrical will be from the 
existing building to the new site. They are requesting a waiver from the site plan regulations to allow 
the continuation of timber curbs within the parking lot.  
 
Chair Woodfin asked how the panels will be pointed and if can see from Portsmouth St.  
 
Ms. Dunson noted the panels will be pointed towards the Board and will not be visible from 
Portsmouth St.  
 
There being no public testimony, Chair Woodfin closed the public hearing. 
 
Chair Woodfin stated the findings of fact include the information provided in the staff reports; the 
applicant’s submission materials; testimony provided during the public hearing; and/or other 
documents or materials provided in the public hearing.  
 
On a motion made by Member Hicks, seconded by Member Condodemetraky, the Board voted 9-0-0 
to grant the waiver requests below from the listed sections of the Site Plan Regulations, based on 
evidence provided showing that the criteria of RSA 674:44(III)(e) and Section 36.08 of the Site Plan 
Regulations are met: 
a. Section 18.19 Curbing and Guardrails, to allow the use of timber curbing, similar to the 
existing conditions on site, where otherwise granite curbing would be required. 
 
On a motion made by Member Hicks, seconded by Member Wilber, the Board voted 9-0-0 to grant 
the amendment to the approved site plan for the proposed ground mounted solar photovoltaic 
array, relocated parking, and associated site improvements at Tax Map 482Z Lot 14, addressed as 52-
54 Portsmouth Street, subject to the following precedent and subsequent conditions: 
(a) Precedent Conditions - to be fulfilled within one year and prior to signature of the final plat by 
the Planning Board Chair and Clerk, unless otherwise specified: 
1. The cover sheet or site plan notes shall be revised to list all approvals, variances, waivers, and

Parking and Loading. 
 
Mr. Thompson summarized the proposed amendments, which will provide significantly increased 
flexibility for relief from the regulatory requirements associated with parking, loading, and driveway 
access. The shift of the majority of design standards to the Site Plan Regulations allows the use of 
waivers, a less stringent statutory standard of relief, administered by the Planning Board, eliminating 
most of the need to seek variance relief from the Zoning Board of Adjustment. For the minority of

permit relief valves, again putting administration of relief in the hands of the Planning Board rather 
than the ZBA. Lastly, these zoning and regulation amendments eliminate the challenges associated 
with differing standards that exist today between the regulations and Zoning Ordinance.
